title: Recognizing a stack from an action-groupoid cover
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $H$ a finite group, and $U$ an $S$-scheme with a left $H$-action. Write $H_T=\coprod_{h\in H}T$ for the constant group scheme over an $S$-scheme $T$. Let $\mathcal Z$ be a stack in groupoids for the etale topology, in the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $a:U\to\mathcal Z$ be a morphism with the following local lifting property: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $z\in\mathcal Z(T)$ there are a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $T_i\to T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], maps $u_i:T_i\to U$, and isomorphisms $a(u_i)\simeq z|_{T_i}$. Suppose given isomorphisms $\alpha_{h,u}:a(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(hu)$, functorial in the test scheme, satisfying $\alpha_{1,u}=1$ and $\alpha_{g,hu}\alpha_{h,u}=\alpha_{gh,u}$. Suppose that the morphism
$$H_S\times_SU\longrightarrow U\times_{\mathcal Z}U,\qquad(h,u)\longmapsto(u,hu,\alpha_{h,u})$$
is an isomorphism, where the right side is the 2-fibre product: for every $S$-scheme $T$ it is an equivalence from the set $(H_S\times_SU)(T)$, viewed as a discrete groupoid, to the fibre of the 2-fibre product over $T$ (a groupoid with at most one arrow between two objects). Then the canonical morphism $[U/H]\to\mathcal Z$, specified on the atlas by $a$ and on arrows by $\alpha$, is an equivalence. Here $[U/H](T)$ is the groupoid of left $H_T$-torsors $P\to T$ and equivariant maps $P\to U$, with equivariant isomorphisms as arrows; a torsor is a $T$-scheme with a left $H_T$-action which, after base change to some jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $T_i\to T$, is equivariantly isomorphic to $H_{T_i}$ with left translation. The equivalence is determined up to unique compatible 2-isomorphism by these specified maps on objects and arrows.

source.place: Tags 04T4 (lemma-map-space-into-stack), 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation), and examples-stacks.tex Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks). The local-lifting version for an etale stack is the same stack-presentation criterion; finite constant group actions allow etale-local trivializations. Agent-formulated criterion with the groupoid identification as an explicit hypothesis.

proof.text: Work on the big etale site of $S$ in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Define the fibred action groupoid $\mathcal A$: objects over $T$ are $u:T\to U$, and arrows $u\to v$ are $h\in H_T(T)$ with $hu=v$. Composition is $(g,h)\mapsto gh$. The prescribed maps give a pullback-compatible functor $A:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, by $u\mapsto a(u)$, $h\mapsto\alpha_{h,u}$. For a nonconstant section $h:T\to H_S$, restrict to the open-and-closed components on which it is constant and glue the arrows using the isomorphism-sheaf axiom of $\mathcal Z$. The given identities imply the functor laws on these components, hence globally. The assumed equivalence $H_S\times_SU\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ identifies, for fixed $u,v$, the entire arrow presheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A}(u,v)$ with $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Z}(a(u),a(v))$. It is therefore already an etale sheaf.

source.place: Tag 04T4 (lemma-map-space-into-stack), description of fibre triples and composition; here representability of the relation is an explicit hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] to obtain $i:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Q=a_{et}\mathcal A$. The universe-small skeleton is the one fixed in step 1. Since $\mathcal Z$ is an etale stack, $A$ extends to $F:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Z$ with $Fi\cong A$. For atlas objects $i(u),i(v)$, the same cited statement identifies their isomorphism sheaf with the sheafification of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A}(u,v)$. Step 1 shows this presheaf is already the isomorphism sheaf in $\mathcal Z$, so $F$ induces a bijection on these isomorphisms.

For any $x,y\in\mathcal Q(T)$, the local-object assertion of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] provides a common etale refinement on which both are isomorphic to atlas objects. Step 2 then makes the map of their isomorphism sheaves bijective locally. To see bijectivity on $T$, lift a target isomorphism on that refinement; local injectivity makes the lifts agree on overlaps, and the sheaf condition glues them uniquely. Thus $F$ is fully faithful. Every object of $\mathcal Z$ is locally $a(u)=F(i(u))$ by the lifting hypothesis of the item. Both $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal Z$ are stacks; [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] therefore makes $F$ an equivalence.

source.place: Tag 046N (lemma-characterize-essentially-surjective-when-ff); local isomorphism-sheaf argument as in examples-stacks.tex Tag 04WM.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal T=[U/H]$ with the scheme-torsor definition of the item. By [lem-sfb-finite-constant-torsor-map-etale-stack], it is an etale stack over this same arbitrary $S$. There is a functor $B:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$: it sends $u$ to $q(u)=(H_T,(k,t)\mapsto k u(t))$ and an arrow $h:u\to v$ to $R_{h^{-1}}:k\mapsto kh^{-1}$. Indeed $(kh^{-1})v=ku$, and $R_{g^{-1}}\circ R_{h^{-1}}=R_{(gh)^{-1}}$. These formulas hold on every test scheme and commute with pullback. Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] again to extend $B$ to $E:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal T$, with $Ei\cong B$.

source.place: Tag 0370 (lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids); Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), definition of the functor on trivial torsors.

proof.text: An equivariant $T$-isomorphism $r:H_T\to H_T$ is determined on every test scheme by $c=r(1)\in H_T(T)$, since $r(k)=kc$. For it to define $q(u)\to q(v)$ one needs $cv=u$. Writing $h=c^{-1}$, this is exactly $v=hu$, and $r=R_{h^{-1}}$. Thus $B$ identifies all arrow presheaves between atlas objects. They are sheaves by step 1. The isomorphism-sheaf assertion and local-object assertion of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], followed by the explicit sheaf gluing argument of step 3, show that $E$ is fully faithful. Every $(P,f)\in\mathcal T(T)$ admits an etale trivialization $P|_{T_i}\cong H_{T_i}$ by the definition of torsor. On it put $u_i=f(1)$; equivariance gives $f(k)=ku_i$, so $(P,f)|_{T_i}\cong q(u_i)$. The local-equivalence criterion [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] applies and makes $E$ an equivalence.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), calculation of right translations and local essential surjectivity; stacks.tex Tag 046N.

proof.text: Choose an inverse of $E$ over the base, which exists by step 5, and compose with $F$. This gives $C:\mathcal T\to\mathcal Z$, an equivalence because $E$ and $F$ are equivalences. The comparisons $Ei\cong B$ and $Fi\cong A$ specify $Cq\cong a$ and make the arrow $R_{h^{-1}}$ correspond to $\alpha_{h,u}$; this is exactly the required morphism on the atlas and its action-groupoid arrows. For uniqueness, let $C,C'$ have these specified comparisons. For $(P,f)$ choose an etale trivialization, so it is locally $q(u_i)$. On each piece the comparisons give the required isomorphism $C(P,f)\cong C'(P,f)$. Changes of trivialization are exactly the arrows $R_{h^{-1}}$ computed in step 5; compatibility with the prescribed $\alpha$ makes these local isomorphisms agree on overlaps. The isomorphism sheaf in $\mathcal Z$ glues them uniquely. Naturality holds after trivializing source and target of any arrow, hence globally by the same sheaf axiom. This proves uniqueness of the compatible 2-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), comparison; uniqueness expanded using the stack isomorphism-sheaf axiom.
